llm.summary: The skill is mostly a benchmark/evaluation utility, but it includes under-disclosed scoring and untrusted execution paths with weak containment.

dimensions.detail: The skill may execute untrusted skill code in-process without sandboxing, resource limits, or the documented timeout, and its broad sys.path manipulation can resolve code outside the reviewed artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time hook, package installer, remote payload fetch, or background service was found, but scripts/pareto.py imports an ambient lib.common module from outside the skill artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md says not to use this for candidate scoring, but interfaces/frozen_benchmark.py and interfaces/hidden_tests.py provide scoring and test-execution flows; the hidden test runner also accepts a timeout parameter but does not enforce it.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Local SQLite and JSON writes are expected for a benchmark store, but benchmark_db.py can create an unrequested ./benchmarks.db before honoring the caller's --db-path and includes benchmark deletion.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is a benchmark store and baseline/Pareto reference, while shipped code also runs evaluators, executes skills under test, calculates scores, stores eval_results, and exposes hidden-test management APIs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only in a controlled benchmark environment. Do not use this as a trusted hidden-test or untrusted-skill execution runner until it uses vetted authenticated encryption, enforces timeouts and sandboxing, resolves dependencies from a pinned trusted location, and clearly documents its scoring/deletion behavior.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The fixture-stub aspect is not material by itself, but the broader artifact does support a purpose-boundary concern because benchmark-store ships evaluator execution and scoring code despite saying candidate scoring belongs elsewhere.
[PE3] expected: The /etc/passwd and /etc/shadow strings appear as adversarial path-traversal test inputs in red-team documentation and test cases, not as code that reads credential files.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The bundled data and defaults include general skill-evaluator cases and skill capability reporting, which is broader than a narrowly scoped benchmark storage/reference skill.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The hidden-test API uses SHA-256 plus repeating-key XOR for protected test data and can return full HiddenTest objects, which undermines the claimed hidden/encrypted test boundary.
[LP3] expected: No install-time permissions manifest was present; this is a disclosure gap, but not by itself evidence of malicious behavior.
[SQP-3] expected: Most user-facing content is Chinese; this is a localization/usability issue rather than evidence of hidden or unsafe behavior.
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger text is in fixture sample skills used as benchmark material, not the primary installed skill instructions.
[T08] unexpected: scripts/pareto.py prepends a high-level ancestor directory to sys.path and imports lib.common that is not bundled in the artifact, creating an external code-resolution risk.
[T09] unexpected: The cryptography, timeout, sandboxing, and unrequested database creation findings are supported by the artifact and are material implementation risks, though they do not show exfiltration or destructive malware.
